newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Aramco invites bids for gas project.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco invites bids for gas project.

text.p: Saudi Aramco has invited bids to lay a 375 million riyals ($100 million), 652-km gas pipeline to link its Hawiyah field to a power station outside Riyadh, the Saudi Gazette newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The pipeline tender is one of five packages for the 7.5 billion riyals Hawiyah gas processing plant project, the largest expansion of gas processing in Saudi Arabia for a decade.
The main 3.375 billion riyals engineering, procurement and construction contract was tendered in May. Project manager, under a contract awarded in 1996, is U.S. engineers Parsons.
Hawiyah processing plant will be able to process 1.44 billion cubic feet a day of gas and is expected to come on stream in 2002-2003.
Aramco is developing its gas fields to keep pace with rising domestic power and water desalination needs.

In addition to Hawiyah it has or is in the process of expanding capacity at its Uthmaniyyah, Berri and Shedgum gas facilities which form the backbone of the country's master gas system (MGS), according to industry sources.
Hawiyah is part of Aramco's super-giant Ghawar field.
